sermon.title: What Is the Church?
sermon.speaker: Guest speaker at Vine Cluster Church (name not given in the recording)
sermon.summary: In this message a speaker at Vine Cluster Church teaches that the church is a people called out of darkness, built on Jesus Christ as its foundation, and given authority and a calling that angels and principalities watch. He goes through what the church does when it gathers (praise, prayer, ministering to the Lord, fasting), the qualities it should show the world, and closes with Philippians 3: the goal is to know Christ now.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: this message is not spoken by Pastor David G. Kincer; the speaker refers to him as “our pastor” and as being away, and the speaker is not named in the captions. Several people are mentioned by first name or title as they appear in the captions; their names are left in the transcript only. The caption “Mr. Kincer”-type spellings (“kiner,” “kcer,” “piner”) were normalized to “Mr. Kincer.” He says “1 Corinthians 3:1” in the captions where the quoted words are 1 Corinthians 3:11 (corrected); “Matthew 18:1. 17” was corrected to Matthew 18:17. He says “Hebrews 2:12” and notes that the words come from a Psalm (Psalm 22:22). The line “Judge righteous judgment” is not given with a reference (John 7:24). Several caption slips were corrected (“cor” to “cornerstone,” “deepens” to “defense,” “hil” to “hell,” “reer” to “receive her,” “command” to “commend”). One spot is marked [unclear]. Statements about angels of the church, “God stepping down,” the Catholic Church and Protestant leaders are the speaker’s own and are not verified here.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean that the church is called out of darkness, and why do believers in China risk prison to gather? (1 Peter 2:9)
chunks.short_answer: He says the church “is a people that’s called out of sin and to his light, and the light exposes us,” and you can’t live as a Christian thinking you can stay in darkness. He points to churches in China where people put their lives on the line just to gather, and says “we should have that same desire in America. It’s scriptural, it’s important.”

He’s called us out of darkness. he The church is a people that’s called out of sin and to his light, and the light exposes us. How do we know? With these lights on you can see things. I can see Christina, she’s got a stain on her jacket. Just kidding. And people, the Bible says that people don’t like the light because it exposes them. That’s right. That God has called us out of darkness, I mean, these scriptures make it plain. You can’t live your life as a Christian thinking that you you can stay in darkness. No way.

Why are the churches in China risking their lives, risking prison, to gather? The unofficial church. Mr. Kincer, our pastor, is over there right now cuz he wants to see what’s happening, he wants to be a part. You know, those people are are putting their lives on the line just to gather. You know, they could all stay home. They’re not taking the excuse, “I’m just going to stay home and live for Jesus.” They’re putting everything on the line together. And why? Is it ignorance because they’re just ignorant people? No, they have something inside of them that wants to gather with God’s people, and we should have that same desire in America. It’s scriptural, it’s important.

chunks.short_answer: He says that in Matthew 16:18 Jesus “talking about himself. He’s going to build the church on himself,” not on Peter, John, James or the apostles. He says “Jesus is the rock,” the word has not changed in 2,000 years, and he wants “a sure foundation” rather than a philosophy that can be proven wrong.

And we’re going to go back to the verse that we talked about, Matthew 16:18, and he says, “Thou art Peter.” Now Peter, the word means piece of a rock, “and upon this rock.” This rock, you know, nonverbal communication is so helpful. You know, if we had a video of Jesus and Peter talking, it would be very helpful, you know, because this is what Jesus would be doing. Okay, say I’m Jesus and Peter’s standing here, “Thou art Peter, and upon this rock,” that’s what he’s saying. You know, I’ve read the scripture several times and you always think he’s talking about Peter. No, he’s talking about himself. He’s going to build the church on himself. And we know that’s true in 1 Corinthians 3:11, it says, “For no other foundation can anyone lay than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.” He is the rock. He didn’t say which is Peter, which is John, which is James. he said He didn’t say the apostles. He said the foundation is Jesus Christ. He’s building the church on himself. In Isaiah 28:16 it says, “I lay in Zion, I lay...”

And you read right through that, but he’s saying, “I’m laying down in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation.” And how many know, when when you build a building you better have a good foundation. People try to build their lives on their own philosophies. “I can live the way I want, I can do something as long as I don’t Hur you know I can do this as long as I don’t hurt somebody.” We have our own philosophies, but Jesus’s philosophy is the foundation. chunks.section_question: What are the gates of hell, and what should the church do about them? (Matthew 16:18)
chunks.short_answer: He says the gates are “defense” and an entryway, and “the entryway to hell is sin.” He says sin and hell can look good on the first level, “but you don’t know that there’s a second level under there,” and that the church should be attacking the gates so they do not reach young people or America.
chunks.text:
That’s our foundation, Jesus Christ. And we have an enemy. It goes on to say that the gates of hell shall not provoke shall not prevail against it. And the gates, as we know, you put up gates or a wall as a defense, and it’s an entryway also. And the entryway to hell is sin. We know that if you want to get into hell, there’s a way get in, no problem: sin. And you know, the the first level of hell, when you look at it, it’s not like it’s black and dark and scary. No, hell doesn’t look bad. You look at the level of hell and it’s like, “Wow, they’re having a good time.” You know, hell looks good, sin looks good, the alcohol and the drugs, they all look good, the the sexual immorality, it looks good and it feels good. But you don’t know that there’s a second level under there, and you don’t know that the third level bottoms out, and the only thing under it is the lake of fire.

Gates are defense, because the church is... we should be attacking the gates of hell. We don’t want them reaching our young people, we don’t want them reaching our generation, we don’t want them overtaking America. Like we learned last week, some of us Americans are sick and we need healing. We’re sick, we need we need a spiritual medicine. We’ve been overcome by doctrines that people have taught us that sin is okay, and it’s not. We’ve got to get back on the right track.

chunks.section_question: How should we treat God’s people, who are the body of Christ? (Acts 9:4, Matthew 25)
chunks.short_answer: He says that when Jesus asked Saul “Why are you persecuting me?” and said “I was sick, I was thirsty, I was hungry,” it shows “there is no separation between me and God’s people.” He says we should treat each other, and our spouses, the way we treat Jesus, “with love, with respect, with kindness, with patience,” and think before we speak.
chunks.text:
The church as the body. Last week we learned when Saul was on the road to Damascus and Jesus stopped him and he said, “Why are you persecuting me?” And in Matthew 25 it says he goes on to say, “For I was sick, I was thirsty, I was hungry,” and he’s saying right there, there is no separation between me and God’s people. people And you know, that’s like I said before, when I came in here after reading these scriptures, you know, how are we treating God’s people? are we We need to treat them the way we treat Jesus Christ. We should be treating our W our our spouses the way that we treat Jesus Christ. We should come in here to our brethren with love, with respect, with kindness, with patience.

When you talk to Jesus, you talk to him with with with humbleness, right? You know, you don’t come up and slap in the face. And what you what do you do? What do you think? You know, super uh you just don’t, you don’t hold anything back when you make a critical statement, you just beat them to a pole. That’s not the way we should do it. chunks.section_question: What does it mean to rule your house well and command respect? (1 Timothy 3:4)
chunks.short_answer: He says we should love one another “where each other are at” and be patient. On “having his children in subjection with all gravity,” he says it means someone who “commands respect because of their character, because of their dignity.” He says parents should demand respect not by using their voice but by living a life of dignity and character.
chunks.text:
Ah, you know, we can’t come in this church church and rail on each other because we’re at a certain place, and you can’t use that as an excuse to stay where you’re at. One that rules his own house well, and this is important. When I looked up the word here, “having his children in subjection with all gravity,” King James, and I looked at that word, I’m like, “What is he talking about?” You know, and I looked up the English word for this, and it’s a word I’ve never heard before. And when I looked it up, he’s talking about a father or a parent, a mother, someone who commands respect because of their character, because of their dignity, because of the virtue that is inside of them. You know, this is talking about a bishop or or a an elder, someone that the church looks up to. You know, we should all be having these goals to be like this. We should all, as parents, you know, not demanding your the respect using your voice, but demanding respect because you are living a life that is so dignified, so you have such character.

chunks.section_question: What does Romans 16:1-2 say about receiving and assisting those who serve? (Romans 16:1-2)
chunks.short_answer: He cites Paul’s words about Phoebe as an example of a woman who was put in charge, and says to treat her “as becometh saints,” with patience and kindness and not condescendingly. He says even if you are not “super Christian,” you can help and assist those who are working to get things done, because “we need assistance, and we all can put our hand in.”
chunks.text: Romans 16:1-2, “I commend unto you Phoebe our sister.” And I bring this up because we this is a good example of where a woman was put in charge, and Paul said, “Receive her in the Lord as becometh saints.” You know, receive her in the Lord, as the way you would treat treat me as a saint, the way you would treat me. You talk to her, you don’t talk to her down, you don’t talk to her condescendingly, you talk to her right, you talk to her with patience and kindness. And amen, you didn’t say talk to her like she’s a woman. Talk to her with love, talk to her with respect, “as becometh saints. Assist her in whatever business she have need of you.” You know, just because you’re a woman doesn’t mean you get to be in charge, but just because you’re a woman doesn’t mean that you can’t, get you know, be sent by Paul. it It happened back there, and in other cases as well. “A sister, or whatever business she,” you know, maybe we don’t want to be in, maybe you can’t, you know, maybe you’re not someone who’s super Christian. Okay, maybe you’re someone that’s still being transformed, but you can help, and you can assist the people that are in charge, like Christina, like Mr. Kincer, like Mr. Barnes, and these people that are working and trying to get things done. chunks.section_question: What else does the Bible say the church is: light, salt, a royal priesthood and an army?
chunks.short_answer: He says we are “the light of the world,” “the salt of the earth,” “a royal priesthood, a chosen generation,” and an army that fights “for his word,” “for truth.” He quotes Jesus, “My kingdom is not of this world,” and says “the church is more.”
chunks.text:
You know, we have two young people that are here to help my wife with the horses today. that you know Thank you. They’re here to assist. That’s good. And like I said, this is not sum up the church, there’s more. The Bible says that we are the light of the world, we are the salt of the earth. You can just go on and on and on. We’re the joy of the whole earth. You know, we walk in here, we’re supposed to have some joy in our hearts. Why? Because we know Jesus, because we met him throughout the week. We’ve got him inside of Christ in you. We’ve got joy. We’re the salt of the earth. scriptures.text_nkjv: “You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt loses its flavor, how shall it be seasoned? It is then good for nothing but to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by men. “You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden.
But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light;
Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not of this world. If My kingdom were of this world, My servants would fight, so that I should not be delivered to the Jews; but now My kingdom is not from here.”

Pilate therefore said to Him, “Are You a king then?” Jesus answered, “You say rightly that I am a king. For this cause I was born, and for this cause I have come into the world, that I should bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears My voice.” Pilate said to Him, “What is truth?” And when he had said this, he went out again to the Jews, and said to them, “I find no fault in Him at all.

chunks.section_question: What is the goal of the Christian life: to know Christ? (Philippians 3:8-10)
chunks.short_answer: He reads Philippians 3:8 and says there will come a day when the things you did not want to give up for Christ, such as the time and discipline to read God’s word, will look like “rubbish.” He reads Philippians 3:10 and says “our goal is to know Jesus, and we don’t have to wait till we die and go to heaven,” because Jesus is saying “you can know me now.”
chunks.text:
Philippians 3:8, “Doubtless I count all things but lost for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung,” poop, potty. “I count it all rubbish, worthless.” You know, there’s going to come a day in your Christian walk where the things that you didn’t want to give up for Christ, the time that you didn’t want to give up, the the time it takes to to read God’s word, the discipline it takes, the discipline that you didn’t want to give up, there’s going to come a time where, when you transform, when when you decide to give up those things, you’re going to look back on it and it’s going to be rubbish. Dung, “that you might win Christ.” See, that’s the goal. We want to win Christ, the glory of God.

Philippians 3:10, he goes on to say, “That I may know him and the power of his resurrection.” That I might know Jesus Christ. Church, we our goal is to know Jesus, and we don’t have to wait till we die and go to heaven. You see, the the the story of Jesus and his bride implies that you have to wait to be married to him before you can know him, but Jesus is saying, you can commit to you to me now, you can know me now.

faqs.question: Does he say the church is built on Peter?
faqs.answer: He says no: “you always think he’s talking about Peter. No, he’s talking about himself. He’s going to build the church on himself.” He says Jesus “didn’t say the apostles. He said the foundation is Jesus Christ.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For no other foundation can anyone lay than that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

faqs.question: What does he mean by a “falsifiable” philosophy?
faqs.answer: He says a college science teacher told his class that everything taught is “falsifiable,” meaning it can be proven wrong. He says no one should base their life on that, but on the sure answer, Jesus Christ.

faqs.question: Does he say God’s word changes?
faqs.answer: He says “no matter how many generations come and go, Jesus is always the same,” and that his word “hasn’t changed” in 2,000 years, which is why it is “a sure foundation.”

faqs.question: Why does he say sin looks good?
faqs.answer: He says the first level of hell doesn’t look “black and dark and scary” but looks like people having a good time. He says the alcohol, drugs and sexual immorality “it looks good and it feels good,” but there is a second level, a third level, and under it the lake of fire.

faqs.question: What does he say we need to get back on track?
faqs.answer: He says “we need a spiritual medicine” because we have been “overcome by doctrines that people have taught us that sin is okay, and it’s not.” He says “we’ve got to get back on the right track.”

faqs.question: What does he say to do when someone in the church offends you?
faqs.answer: He describes going to talk to them first, then taking someone with you if they refuse to listen, and then bringing it before the church. He says Jesus is not saying to take it to a judge in a court.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And if he refuses to hear them, tell it to the church. But if he refuses even to hear the church, let him be to you like a heathen and a tax collector.

faqs.question: Can Christians judge?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus said bring it before the church, and that “One day we’re going to judge the whole world,” and asks why we can’t do what’s right now. He says we need to “judge righteous judgment.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world will be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?

faqs.question: How does he say we should speak to each other and to Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says when you talk to Jesus you talk with humbleness and you would “think before you speak.” He says we shouldn’t make critical statements that “beat them to a pole.”

faqs.question: Does he say a Christian is changed instantly?
faqs.answer: He says “you don’t pop yourself in the microwave and you come out super Christian.” He says it is “line upon line,” “here a little, there a little,” and that God is transforming you and it takes time.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept, Line upon line, line upon line, Here a little, there a little.”

faqs.question: What does he say it means to minister to the Lord?
faqs.answer: He says people in the church come thinking they are there to get something from God, when God says “you guys minister to me,” not because he needs it but “because he knows what happens to you when you minister to him.” He says they ministered and fasted.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now in the church that was at Antioch there were certain prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

faqs.question: What does he say about wanting to meet famous people?
faqs.answer: He says we would rather talk to a famous person, but “we have an opportunity for Jesus to be inside of us and not only inside of us but doing something powerful through us.” He says “Jesus is the famous one.”

faqs.question: What does he say it means to count things as rubbish?
faqs.answer: He says there will come a time in your Christian walk when you give up the things you did not want to give up for Christ, and “it’s going to be rubbish.” He says the goal is to win Christ.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Yet indeed I also count all things loss for the excellence of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and count them as rubbish, that I may gain Christ

faqs.question: Does he say we have to wait until heaven to know Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says “we don’t have to wait till we die and go to heaven,” and that Jesus is saying “you can know me now.”
